ideas.title: Android SMS warning — observe and warn, since blocking is impossible
ideas.description:
FUTURE ADDITION. Not in release 1. Release 1 ships SMS filtering on iPhone only.

WHAT IT WOULD DO
Android listens for incoming SMS, runs the same rules from the shared core, and warns the user when a message matches. The message still arrives in their messaging app. We cannot stop it.

WHY BLOCKING IS IMPOSSIBLE (verified 2026-09-08 by reading android-36 sources, P001(F001)/T002)
android/provider/Telephony.java, verbatim:
"Only the default SMS app (selected by the user in system settings) is able to write to the SMS Provider ... and only the default SMS app receives the SMS_DELIVER_ACTION broadcast"
"Other apps that are not selected as the default SMS app can only read the SMS Provider, but may also be notified when a new SMS arrives by listening for the SMS_RECEIVED_ACTION broadcast, which is a NON-ABORTABLE broadcast"

Non-default apps observe. They never block. Becoming the default SMS app would require handling SMS_DELIVER, WAP_PUSH_DELIVER (MMS), ACTION_SENDTO and RESPOND_VIA_MESSAGE — a complete messaging application with conversations, MMS, drafts, notifications and search. That is a different product, and it is the same line iOS draws with TelephonyMessagingKit, already out of scope.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN RELEASE 1
1. It needs RECEIVE_SMS, which puts the app into Google Play's restricted SMS permission group. That means a Permissions Declaration Form and a Play review that can be refused. Release 1 avoids that queue entirely and has no dependency outside our control.
2. The value is weak. A warning after the message has already arrived is barely better than the user reading the message. Blocking is what people want, and it is unavailable.
3. It creates an asymmetry that is hard to explain: the same rule blocks on iPhone and only warns on Android. R8 already carries a long list of platform differences the UI must present honestly; this adds another for little gain.
4. Release 1 is deliberately narrow: user-authored rules, no servers, no restricted permissions, nothing waiting on a reviewer.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT WORTH DOING
- Users asking for it after release 1, rather than us guessing they want it.
- A Play declaration already approved for another reason, so the review cost is already paid.
- Evidence that a warning changes behaviour — for example if paired with a one-tap block of the sender's number for future CALLS, which Android can do.

DEPENDENCIES IF PICKED UP
- The rule engine already handles it: iOS SMS filtering in release 1 proves the same evaluate() path against a sender and a message body. No core work.
- Needs the Android SMS receiver, the Play declaration, and a warning UI.
- Would require amending R2, which currently promises SMS filtering on both platforms.

RELATED: P012(F005) holds the full analysis and the three options. Option 3 there — building a full messaging app — remains rejected as out of proportion.
